subject: Re: Throughput & SLO qualification — tokens/sec and streaming requirements
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@finex.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: throughput & streaming notes

Rafael / team — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and the numbers we discussed so you can validate sizing on your side. Attaching our workload snapshot (finex_workload_snapshot.csv).

Summary: 
- Steady-state: ~120 requests/sec, each request ~60 tokens on average (mostly short summaries). That maps to ~7.2k tokens/sec steady.
- Peak bursts: up to 350 requests/sec for 3–5 minute windows (end-of-day batch activities) — roughly 21k tokens/sec peak.
- Concurrency: we currently have ~250 simultaneous active users during peaks; typical session generates 2 concurrent calls.
- Streaming: ~45% of calls use streaming (progressive summary), rest are non-streaming single-response calls.
- Latency expectation: p95 under 300ms for non-streaming; streaming needs first-byte <200ms and steady chunk <100ms ideally.

Questions for you: what sizing do you recommend for predictable p95 latency at peak? Also curious how you handle bursty loads (autoscale, queueing, fallback).

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Head of Integrations — FinEx Capital
Attachments: finex_workload_snapshot.csv (CSV, 120KB)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: throughput & streaming notes

Alex — great notes, this is very helpful. A few clarifying items so we size correctly: 

1) Latency SLOs: you called out p95 <300ms for non-streaming and first-byte <200ms for streaming. Are those firm SLOs for production, or targets we should treat as aspirational for phase-1? Also, what's your p99 target (if any)?

2) Token distribution: average 60 tokens is fine, but do you have percentile distribution (p50/p90/p99 token length)? That changes batching efficiency.

3) Traffic shape: the 350 rps peak — is that single sustained peak or repeated multiple times/day? Also confirm burst growth rate (how fast does it ramp up).

4) Streaming behavior: are streaming calls long-running (100s of tokens) or short progressive chunks? And is partial output acceptable if we fall back to shorter responses during extreme overload?

I'll loop in Marissa and Marcus to give a preliminary sizing suggestion. Attaching an initial sizing worksheet and rough recommendation (redwood_sizing_recommendation_v1.pdf).

Would you be available for a 30-min follow-up review on Thursday (8/6) to go over the recommended topology and cost tradeoffs?

—Rafael
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_sizing_recommendation_v1.pdf (PDF, 480KB)

From: Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: throughput & streaming notes

Hi Rafael / Marissa — quick answers from our ops side: 

- Latency targets: p95 = 250–300ms is firm for non-streaming; p99 we target <600ms but can tolerate short blips during rare infra incidents.
- Token percentiles: p50=48, p90=120, p99=420 (a small number of very long analyst queries).
- Peak pattern: the 350 rps events are typically hourly spikes during market closes (3–6 times/day) and one bigger daily end-of-day batch that lasts ~4 minutes. Ramp-up is usually <30s.
- Streaming: streaming calls send chunks every ~150–300ms; average streaming total length ~250 tokens but first-byte latency is most important. If you need to degrade, partial streaming with a final summary is acceptable.

Happy to confirm on the follow-up call 8/6 — 10:00am PT works for us.

Thanks,
Sophie Lee
Platform Ops — FinEx Capital

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>, Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@finex.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput & SLO qualification — preliminary sizing

Alex / Sophie / Rafael — thanks for the details. Based on the snapshot and Sophie’s percentiles, here's a conservative preliminary sizing and operational notes (sending high-level bullets here; attached is the PDF with numbers):

- Model choice: a quantized 7B variant with streaming-optimized runtime (mix of attention kernels) should meet latency targets with good cost/throughput tradeoff.
- Steady-state capacity: design for 120 rps -> ~8k tokens/sec. One 8x A100-equivalent pool (with optimized batching) should handle steady traffic with headroom.
- Peak capacity and burst handling: for 21k tokens/sec peak and <30s ramp, recommend a hybrid approach: 
  - Reserved pool sized for 2x steady (~16k tokens/sec)
  - Autoscale burst workers that warm on short notice (GPU pool with fast startup) to cover additional ~5k tokens/sec; also enable graceful queueing with SLA-aware routing.
- Concurrency: target 500 concurrent request slots across the cluster to keep p95 stable; implement KV prefix caching for repeated prompts.
- Streaming: prioritize first-byte by pinning warm workers for streaming subset (45% of traffic). Configure smaller micro-batches for streaming requests to reduce first-byte latency (target <200ms).
- Fallbacks: configure automatic fallback to a smaller model variant for non-critical requests and circuit-breaker policy when queue latency exceeds threshold.

Next steps: review numbers on Thu 8/6 10:00am PT (invite sent). After the call we’ll turn the PDF into an ops runbook and a mutual action plan with milestones (POC, perf tests, go/no-go).

—Marissa Cole
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_sizing_recommendation_v1.pdf (PDF, 480KB); link: https://drive.redwood.com/finex/sizing-notes
